name: Ginger K. Gooch
description: Concurred, argued that the plain language of the Missouri Constitution does not provide for automatic suspension of a legislative act merely upon the filing of a referendum petition, but requires the signature requirement to be met and the petition to be certified as sufficient through the statutory process.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Concurred, argued that the Appellants failed to demonstrate that the 2025 Map clearly and undoubtedly violates the Missouri Constitution's requirements for compactness, contiguity, and equal population.

name: Zel M. Fischer
description: Concurred, argued that Article III, section 45 does not limit the General Assembly's power to redistrict more frequently than once a decade, as 'when' does not mean 'only when'.

name: Paul C. Wilson
description: Dissented, argued that Article III, section 45 was intended to limit the General Assembly's authority to redistrict only after each decennial census, and the word 'when' implies 'only when'.

name: Ransom, J.
description: Dissented, concurring with Judge Wilson's opinion that Article III, section 45 limits redistricting to decennial census periods.

name: Russell, J.
description: Dissented, concurring with Judge Wilson's opinion that Article III, section 45 limits redistricting to decennial census periods.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Concurred, argued that Appellants lacked standing to challenge HB 1878, thus the circuit court's alternative merits determination must be reversed.

name: Zel M. Fischer
description: Concurred in result only, arguing that the parties proved organizational standing and the circuit court's judgment on the merits, finding HB 1878 constitutional, should be affirmed.

name: Ransom
description: Concurred with the opinion of Judge Fischer.

name: Wilson
description: Concurred with the opinion of Judge Fischer.

name: Mary R. Russell
description: Concurred, argued that the challenged provisions impermissibly restrict core political speech and are not narrowly tailored to any compelling state interest, thus violating the Missouri Constitution.

name: Ginger K. Gooch
description: Dissented, arguing that three of the challenged provisions in section 115.205.1 regulate non-expressive conduct and are constitutional under rational-basis review, while agreeing that the provision in section 115.279.2 is unconstitutional.

name: Fischer, J.
description: Dissented, concurring in the opinion of Gooch, J.

name: Broniec, J.
description: Dissented, concurring in the opinion of Gooch, J.

name: Janet Sutton
description: Concurred, argued that HJR 73 met the single-subject rule but its ballot language was insufficient and unfair, requiring the court to certify new language.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Concurred, argued that SB 22 violated the original purpose requirement of the Missouri Constitution because the amendment to section 526.010 was not germane to the bill's initial purpose related to ballot summaries, and the offending provision could not be severed.

name: KELLY C. BRONIEC
description: Concurred, argued that the SAFE Act and Medicaid ban are constitutionally valid under rational-basis review, as they classify based on age and medical use, serve a legitimate state interest in safeguarding minors, and do not infringe on fundamental rights.

name: Paul C. Wilson
description: Concurred, argued that the Attorney General's review power is limited to the legal content and form of fiscal note summaries, not the substance of the fiscal impact assessment.

name: Mary R. Russell
description: Concurred, argued that the plain language of the Missouri Constitution defines "local government" differently for incorporated and unincorporated areas, limiting a county's authority to impose the sales tax on non-medical marijuana to unincorporated areas only.

name: Zel. M Fischer
description: Dissented, argued that the plain text of the Missouri Constitution defines a county as a "local government" in both incorporated and unincorporated areas, allowing counties to impose the three percent sales tax on recreational marijuana in incorporated areas within their borders.

name: Mary R. Russell
description: Concurred, argued that the summary statement and fiscal note summary were not materially inaccurate or misleading and did not constitute an election irregularity sufficient to cast doubt on the election results, thus upholding Proposition A.

name: Ransom, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Court lacks original jurisdiction over election contests of this nature, but agreed with the dismissal of single subject and clear title claims for lack of jurisdiction.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Concurred, argued that section 116.050.2(2) applies only to constitutional provisions the proposed amendment would repeal, not statutes, and that the statute only requires identifying text explicitly sought to be repealed or modified, not impliedly affected provisions.

name: Kelly C. Broniec
description: Dissented, argued that Amendment 3 failed to comply with section 116.050.2(2) by not including all statutes and constitutional provisions that would be repealed by the measure, as the term "repeal" applies to both.

name: Fischer, J.
description: Dissented, concurred with Judge Broniec's dissenting opinion.

name: Gooch, J.
description: Dissented, concurred with Judge Broniec's dissenting opinion.

name: Zel M. Fischer
description: Concurred, argued that the Governor has absolute constitutional discretion over clemency, a reprieve creates no rights and can be rescinded, and Williams has no due process right to the board of inquiry process.

name: Paul C. Wilson
description: Concurred, argued that the fiscal note summary on the ballot for Amendment No. 4 was materially inaccurate and misleading, justifying a new election.

name: Ginger K. Gooch
description: Concurred that the Court has original jurisdiction based on stare decisis, but dissented on the merits, arguing Lucas failed to meet the burden to show the ballot title was insufficient or unfair and did not comply with filing requirements.

name: Fischer, J
description: Concurred with Judge Gooch's separate opinion, which concurred on jurisdiction but dissented on the merits.

name: Robin Ransom
description: Dissented, arguing the Court lacks original jurisdiction to hear the election contest, as its jurisdiction is confined by the Missouri Constitution to public officer elections, not constitutional amendments.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court's judgment must be affirmed because the State did not appeal the equal protection claim, which provides an independent legal basis for the judgment.

name: Zel M. Fischer
description: Concurred, argued that Article III, Section 23 of the Missouri Constitution unambiguously exempts appropriation bills from the single subject requirement, and previous court decisions holding otherwise are incorrect.

name: KELLY C. BRONIEC, JUDGE
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court correctly found the Senate Map constitutional because compactness takes priority over community preservation, mathematical calculations are appropriate for compactness, and the appellants failed to prove the map unconstitutional or preserve their equal population claim.

name: W. Brent Powell, Judge
description: Dissented, argued that the Appellants preserved their constitutional challenge and that the Senate Map violates the Missouri Constitution by allowing population deviation greater than one percent and failing to preserve communities.

name: Wilson, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Appellants preserved their constitutional challenge and that the Senate Map violates the Missouri Constitution by allowing population deviation greater than one percent and failing to preserve communities.

name: Judge Jason M. Sengheiser
description: Concurred, argued that the challenged abortion provisions, including the total abortion ban and the declaration that life begins at conception, do not violate the Missouri Constitution's Establishment Clauses, as the language is permissible and consistent with historical practices, and the determination of when life begins is not strictly a religious one.

name: KELLY C. BRONIEC
description: Concurred, delivering the opinion of the Court, which found that the unfunded mandate claim was sufficiently pleaded to survive a motion for judgment on the pleadings, but affirmed the constitutionality of SB 26 on all other points.

name: Gooch, J.
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: Paul C. Wilson
description: Concurred, argued that TAFP HB 1606 violated the single subject requirement of the Missouri Constitution because section 67.2300, which addresses homelessness, was not germane to the bill's subject of "political subdivisions," rendering the entire bill invalid.

name: Patricia Breckenridge, Judge
description: Dissented, argued that the principal opinion incorrectly construes Article IV, sections 40-44 in isolation, failing to consider other constitutional provisions that grant the General Assembly the power of appropriation and specify requirements for withdrawing money from the treasury.

name: Powell, J
description: Concurred with the dissenting opinion of Judge Breckenridge.

name: Fischer, J
description: Concurred with the dissenting opinion of Judge Breckenridge.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Concurred, argued that the evidence of abuse was not sufficiently distinct to require more specific jury instructions, thus preserving the defendant's right to a unanimous verdict.

name: Breckenridge, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the circuit court erred by not requiring the jury to unanimously agree on the specific criminal act committed, as evidence showed distinct acts of abuse, thereby violating the defendant's right to a unanimous verdict.

name: Draper, J.
description: Dissented, concurred in the opinion of Breckenridge, J.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court lacked authority to hold the clerk in contempt because the clerk's administrative duties, while statutory, do not affect the court's judicial function of trying and determining cases in controversy, and contempt is not the appropriate mechanism to enforce such tasks.

name: PATRICIA BRECKENRIDGE
description: Concurred, delivering the majority opinion that found parts of the parking statutes unconstitutional for creating duties for municipal offices but held that these invalid provisions were severable from the rest of the statutes.

name: ROBIN RANSOM
description: Concurred, argued that the City's charter notice requirement does not irreconcilably conflict with state statutes because it merely supplements state law and notice requirements have a different origin and purpose than statutes of limitations.

name: Fischer, J.
description: Concurred in result, agreeing with the outcome but not necessarily the majority's reasoning.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Concurred, argued that SB 1007 mandates at-will employment for non-merit state employees, does not violate constitutional collective bargaining or contract rights, and many PAB rules are unauthorized expansions.

name: GEORGE W. DRAPER III
description: Concurred, argued that section 565.091 is not overbroad, there was sufficient evidence to support the second-degree harassment conviction, and sentencing for both offenses did not violate double jeopardy.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court's application of the punitive damages cap did not violate All Star's right to a jury trial, and the reduced award did not violate HALO's due process rights.

name: Mary R. Russell
description: Concurred, argued that the challenged statutes unconstitutionally interfere with and impede the right of referendum by unreasonably shortening the timeframe for petition circulation.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Dissented, argued that Challengers failed to demonstrate the statutes are facially invalid and that circumstances exist where the statutes could be applied constitutionally without impeding the right of referendum.

name: Fischer
description: Dissented, argued that Challengers failed to demonstrate the statutes are facially invalid and that circumstances exist where the statutes could be applied constitutionally without impeding the right of referendum.

name: Zel M. Fischer
description: Concurred, argued that medical negligence is a statutorily created cause of action, allowing the legislature to impose non-economic damage caps without violating the right to trial by jury.

name: George W. Draper III
description: Dissented, argued that the majority opinion allows the legislature to unconstitutionally limit the right to trial by jury by reclassifying common law medical malpractice as a statutory cause of action to re-impose caps previously struck down.

name: Ransom, J.
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: Mary R. Russell
description: Concurred, argued that the exemption for public safety labor organizations in HB 1413 violates equal protection and is not severable, rendering the entire bill void.

name: W. Brent Powell
description: Dissented, argued that the public safety exemption is constitutional and does not warrant invalidating HB 1413.

name: Fischer, J.
description: Dissented, concurred with Judge Powell's dissenting opinion.

name: Patricia Breckenridge
description: Concurred, argued that a rational basis supports the classification scheme of the challenged statutes, the fee is not a tax on Crestwood residents, and section 72.418.2 does not create an unfunded mandate.
